scope: Complementary read-only review of the preserved CalculEclairage implementation; original bytes and x86 remain authoritative.

limitations: This session opens a caller-selected existing Ghidra project through a private copy, without import, auto-analysis or repair scripts. Original analysis completeness and settings are unknown.
The original project is never opened by Ghidra or modified. The private copy is read-only to bridge operations and deleted on close; original executable bytes are never written.

The analysis profile records the selected project content fingerprint and program name. The imported program SHA-256 must match the admitted target; the project may contain caller annotations or earlier edits, which are not fresh REA discoveries.
Default-space addresses use lowercase 0x-prefixed hexadecimal; other address spaces use <percent-encoded-space>:0x<hex>.
Pseudocode is Ghidra decompiler output, not original source and not text-equivalent to Hopper output.
External functions and functions without an analyzable body return null; other decompiler failures remain explicit.
macOS sessions require a matching executable Ghidra native decompiler; REA checks for it but does not build native components or change Gatekeeper quarantine state.
This session uses Ghidra 12.2. The bridge is verified against 12.1.4; other 12.x (>=12.1) builds are accepted and the observed version is reported.

review_notes: The decompiled per-component inverse scaling, zero-quotient target30 and cap255 agree with original assembly and the independent x86 tables.
The strict nearest-distance comparison and cycle exclusion agree with captured complete lookup tables.
The displayed fastcall signature, in_EAX and extraout_ECX are decompiler artifacts: the reviewed original inputs remain EAX=palette pointer and DL=percentage.
This existing-project analysis includes earlier caller annotations; French symbols are retained and are not claimed as new REA discoveries.
